title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
why_read: A dense theoretical analysis of partially trainable neural networks that will mainly interest researchers studying approximation theory rather than practitioners.
analysis: This paper studies networks where only a fraction of parameters are trainable while the rest stay as fixed random features, and it mathematically characterizes a phase transition where a small trainable fraction captures most of the benefit of full training. It derives formal approximation bounds using kernel and spectral decay assumptions, verified for specific feature types like spherical biased-ReLU units. The practical takeaway, that a small trainable proportion can capture 90% of the improvement, is intriguing for efficient training schemes, but the heavy theoretical framing limits its audience mostly to theorists.
